summary.headline: Mixed week: revenue cleared target at 100.4% while orders reached only 95.0%; the year is still behind at 93.0% of target.

points.what: Revenue of $60,547 reached 100.4% of the weekly target, while orders came in at 95.0%.
points.so_what: Revenue met its target without order volume doing so, so the week cannot be read as broadly on target.

points.what: Orders fell 0.5% and revenue 1.3% against the prior week, both rated bad.
points.so_what: The quarter opens slightly below the prior week's level rather than building on it.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue stands at 93.0% of target, $58,749 short.
points.so_what: One week at target leaves the year's position unchanged, and that shortfall carries into Q2.

points.what: Orders grew 51.4% and revenue 44.9% on last year, both below the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is running under the rate the targets were built on, which is how the year-to-date gap has opened.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose to 14.2%, up 0.6 pp on the prior week and 2.1 pp on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: One percentage point of cancellations is worth $706 of revenue, more than the $249 by which revenue cleared target this week.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target requires $79,813 of revenue a week for the rest of the year, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $57,975.
points.so_what: The $3,888,802 full-year target is out of reach at the current pace.

points.what: AOV of $82.94 is down 2.0% on last year, rated bad.
points.so_what: Value per order sits below last year, so revenue has to lean on order counts that are themselves behind target.

points.what: Orders of 851 fell 45 below the weekly target of 896, and next week's target is 854 orders.
points.so_what: The order gap has to close from a base that is already lower than the target it just missed.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is at 100.4% of target, with $823,539 of the $884,086 quarter target still to come over 12 weeks.
points.so_what: Almost the whole quarter is still ahead, so a first-week beat gives very little cushion.

points.what: January, February and March all closed behind target, at 88.0%, 92.4% and 97.7%.
points.so_what: April's above-target start follows three completed months that each added to the year-to-date shortfall.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 9.0% to 111, a contribution of -11 orders and the largest regional drag on the week.
points.so_what: Reading the order decline by region, it concentrates in LATAM rather than being broad-based.

points.what: North America orders rose 7.4% to 202, contributing +14 orders.
points.so_what: North America was the only sizeable regional offset, so the total fell by less than the declining regions alone.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 18.6% to 48, a contribution of -11 orders and the largest drag of any traffic source.
points.so_what: Search's gain of 11 orders did not lift the total above the prior week.

points.what: AOV of $82.94 slipped 0.1% on the prior week, rated bad.
points.so_what: This week's revenue beat came with a smaller average order, so read the revenue figure as volume-led.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 16 Mar 2026 was 9.3%, down 0.2 pp and rated good, and flat on last year.
points.so_what: Returns are not adding to the order-quality pressure coming from cancellations.

points.what: New customer signups rose 9.7% to 259 and were up 10.2% on last year, both rated good.
points.so_what: New accounts grew in a week when orders slipped, so the order dip is not mirrored on the signup side.

points.what: Orders of 851 remain above the recent 8-week average of 790.
points.so_what: Volume is still running above the recent pace even though it came in behind this week's target.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
